body: OCR, layout analysis, reading order, table recognition in 90+ languages
plain_description: Extract text, layout, and tables from any document in 90+ languages with state-of-the-art accuracy. The big picture: Surya turns messy PDFs, scans, and images into clean, structured data — without needing a massive GPU cluster. It handles dense academic papers, handwritten forms, multilingual documents, and complex tables in a single pass. The bottom line: you get production-grade OCR at 5 pages per second on a single GPU, with output you can feed directly into downstream systems.
technical_description: Surya is a 650M-parameter vision-language model for document OCR, layout analysis, reading-order detection, and table recognition. It runs a single shared VLM served by vllm (NVIDIA GPU) or llama.cpp (CPU/Apple Silicon), with a separate torch-based text-line detection model. The Python library provides CLI commands (surya_ocr, surya_layout, surya_table, surya_detect) and a programmatic API via SuryaInferenceManager with RecognitionPredictor, LayoutPredictor, TableRecPredictor, and DetectionPredictor classes. Output is returned as structured JSON with per-block polygons, bboxes, confidence scores, and HTML content (including <math> tags for equations and <table> for recognized tables). The inference manager auto-spawns the backend server or can attach to a pre-running OpenAI-compatible endpoint via SURYA_INFERENCE_URL. A streamlit-based GUI is included for interactive exploration.
title: Surya
